slides.heading: Get it checked if you notice

caption:
Momo's bridges kept landing in her lower back instead of her glutes. Your glutes help control your hips and knees every time you walk, run, climb stairs or lift.

The Pilates approach starts with control, feeling the right muscles work in a slow bridge or clam, then gradually adds load with springs, bands and single-leg work.

Want to start today? Try ten slow bridges, ten clams each side and a 30-second single-leg balance, two or three times a week. If pain builds or tingling spreads down a leg, stop and get it checked.

Our Pilates team at Hybrid Physio starts with an assessment and progresses your program as you get stronger. Book online via the link in bio.
